1. Introduction
Bearings and gearboxes are critical components of rotating machines[1].
These machines often operate under varying speeds, loads, material condi-
tions, maintenance procedures, and environments. Thus, performing effec-
tive fault diagnosis for the equipment through vibrational signal analysis is
challenging and has received significant attention[2].
Intelligent fault diagnosis based on deep learning (DL) has demonstrated
improved performance on fault classification.
Many DL models such as
CNNs [3][4], generative adversarial networks(GANs) [5], Deep Belief Net-
works (DBNs) [6], and transformers [7] are applied in fault diagnosis with
promising results. Among those DL-based methods, the CNN model is de-
veloped to imitate the concept of visual human object recognition. CNN’s
feature extraction performance has been verified in many applications, such
as image recognition [8] and video analysis [9]. There are two main categories
2

of CNN methods used in fault diagnosis depending on the dimensionality of
the input data: two-dimensional CNN (2D-CNN) for processing 2D data
like images[10], and one-dimensional CNN (1D-CNN) for processing 1D data
such as vibrational signals [11]. For the 1D-CNN method, the 1D time series
can be input into the model directly [12]. However, compared with 2D-CNN,
1D-CNN has certain disadvantages when applied to fault diagnosis. First,
raw 1D vibrational signals are usually low separable, and learning features
directly from the 1D signal is relatively inefficient [13]. Existing 1D-to-2D
conversion methods in 2D-CNN models can improve the data separability
and reduce redundancy. Second, the design of 2D-CNN is mature, and many
well-established 2D-CNN models are available in many research literatures.
Meanwhile, the input dimension of 2D-CNN is usually smaller than the 1D-
CNN in fault diagnosis, making the 2D-CNN easier to be designed. Thus,
2D-CNN is studied in this paper.
For the 2D-CNN, the 1D vibrational signal is required to be converted
into a 2D feature representation using various signal processing methods. The
raw signal contains the richest faulty information, but irrelevant information
in the raw signal often limits its separability. The function of the 1D-to-2D
conversion is that it can be regarded as an initial feature extraction procedure
that helps to enhance the convergence of the CNN model [14]. The merits
of the conversion processing include that the converted 2D features usually
contain simpler textures, which are more representative than the raw signals.
For example, Wen et al.[15] transformed a 1D raw vibrational signal into the
2D signal matrix through the tensor reshaping method. The obtained signal
matrices are then fed into the LeNet-5 model for bearing fault diagnosis.

for the wind turbine fault diagnosis. Shao et al.[17] employed the continuous
wavelet transform as the input of the VGG-16 model with the transfer learn-
ing strategy. In [18], the bispectrum of raw vibrational signals is used as the
input of transfer CNN to diagnose the planetary gearbox. In [19] the cyclic
spectral coherence (CSC) connects with a LeNet model for bearing fault
diagnosis because of its ability to exploit the second-order cyclo-stationary

CNN for bearing fault diagnosis. Other representations for encoding time

### Structured Highlights for the Research Paper

#### **Core Innovation**
- **EGR-Net**: A novel convolutional neural network (CNN) that integrates the Embedding Gramian Representation (EGR) for intelligent fault diagnosis in rotating machinery.
- **EGR Method**: A 1D-to-2D conversion technique that projects signals into an embedding space, capturing intrinsic periodicity and enhancing separability.

#### **Technical Approach**
- **EGR Conversion**: Uses embedding space projection to convert 1D signals into 2D feature matrices, improving data representation.
- **Double-Branch CNN**: Employs two branches - one processing raw signals and the other processing EGR features - with a bridge connection for enhanced feature interaction.
- **Bridge Connection**: Facilitates improved feature learning between raw signals and EGR representations, optimizing information flow.

#### **Quantitative Findings**
- **Datasets**: Tested on standard open-domain gearbox and bearing datasets.
- **Performance**: EGR-Net outperforms existing methods, demonstrating enhanced classification accuracy.

#### **Limitations & Assumptions**
- **Datasets**: Limited to open-domain datasets, potentially constraining real-world applicability.
- **Computational Demands**: Requires significant computational resources for processing.
- **Domain Specificity**: Focuses on rotating machinery, assuming similar patterns in other domains.

#### **Domain Impact**
- **Intelligent Fault Diagnosis**: Provides a robust method for identifying faults in rotating machinery.
- **Reduced Information Loss**: Overcomes limitations of previous CNN models by leveraging raw signal features alongside EGR representations.
- **Enhanced Performance**: Demonstrated superior performance, offering a promising advancement in machinery fault diagnosis.
